mcqs.q: Thematic analysis of interviews with Canadian international dog rescue leaders yielded which three themes?
mcqs.e: The study identified Motive, Challenge, and Duty as the three themes.

mcqs.q: Which occupational difficulty did international dog rescue members share with other caregiving professions?
mcqs.e: The emotional burden of caregiving was common to dog rescue and other caregiving work.

mcqs.q: What additional challenge was reported as unique to international (versus local) dog rescue members?
mcqs.e: International rescuers faced added difficulty from the stigma around international operations.

mcqs.q: Compared to domestically acquired rabies in US dogs, the estimated rabies incidence in dogs imported from DMRVV-enzootic countries was approximately:
mcqs.e: Incidence was estimated 16 times higher (range 13.2-19.4) in imported dogs.

mcqs.q: Per the abstract, dog-mediated rabies virus variant has been eliminated from the United States since:
mcqs.e: The abstract states DMRVV has been eliminated from the US since 2007.

mcqs.q: The study's conclusion supports which measure?
o: Importation requirements to prevent reintroduction of DMRVV
mcqs.e: The higher imported-dog risk supports importation requirements to prevent DMRVV reintroduction.

mcqs.q: The "Good Life Frameworks" described were developed for which species?
mcqs.e: Frameworks were built for beef cattle, broiler chickens, and pigs.

mcqs.q: Absent validated animal-based measures, the abstract states the best current way to assess positive welfare is:
mcqs.e: Evaluation of resource provision is considered the best present method.

mcqs.q: The three welfare tiers provide resources that go:
o: Above UK law and code of practice requirements
mcqs.e: Tiers incrementally increase good-life opportunities above legal and code requirements.

mcqs.q: Effective human-goat communication occurs primarily via which stimuli?
mcqs.e: Communication occurs mainly through visual, tactile, and auditory stimuli.

mcqs.q: How many relevant articles were selected in this systematic review?
mcqs.e: The review selected 58 relevant articles.

mcqs.q: Validated measures of human-goat relationship quality included:
o: Avoidance in the pen and latency to first contact
mcqs.e: Avoidance in the pen/feeding rack and latency to first contact were validated measures.

mcqs.q: In farm animals, the review found better animal welfare was generally associated with:
mcqs.e: Better welfare often led to lower antimicrobial use; poor welfare to higher use.

mcqs.q: A potential downside of antimicrobial-use restrictions in organic systems noted by the review:
o: Animals may not receive treatment when necessary
mcqs.e: AMU restrictions may prevent animals from being treated when needed.

mcqs.q: The 16 of 17 retained studies primarily concerned which animals?
mcqs.e: Sixteen of the seventeen retained studies were on farm animals.

mcqs.q: The cluster analysis of noise-anxious horses identified which two groups?
mcqs.e: A two-step cluster analysis produced very anxious (VA) and slightly anxious (SA) groups.

mcqs.q: Horses reporting injuries during noise events were more likely to be classified as:
mcqs.e: Injury during noise events was associated with the very anxious cluster.

mcqs.q: Which management strategy was most likely to be very effective in slightly anxious horses?
mcqs.e: Providing hay overnight was the strategy most likely effective in SA horses.

mcqs.q: What was the most commonly observed welfare issue in the assessed horses?
mcqs.e: Hoof neglect (27%) was the most commonly observed welfare issue.

mcqs.q: What proportion of the horses had an optimal body condition score?
mcqs.e: 81% had optimal body condition, with none very thin or fat.

mcqs.q: Overall, Qualitative Behaviour Assessment indicated the horses' emotional states were:
mcqs.e: Positive emotional states were more common, countering perceptions of poor welfare.

mcqs.q: The commentary recommends emphasizing which type of measure in commercial supply systems?
mcqs.e: Easily assessed animal-based outcome measures should be emphasized.

mcqs.q: Which is given as an example key animal welfare indicator?
o: Percentage of animals effectively stunned with a single application
mcqs.e: Single-application effective stunning percentage is cited as a key indicator.

mcqs.q: A farm that fails to meet specified housing requirements will:
o: Be removed from the approved supplier list
mcqs.e: Non-compliant housing results in removal from the approved supplier list.

mcqs.q: Traditionally, the most common strategies to achieve compliance from horses have been:
o: Physical restraint, punishment, or threat of an aversive
mcqs.e: Physical restraint, punishment, and aversive threats were the traditional strategies.

mcqs.q: A welfare concern of the traditional restraint/punishment approach noted by the review:
o: It may create a more dangerous response in future similar situations
mcqs.e: The approach risks a more dangerous horse response in future encounters.

mcqs.q: The review notes a steady transition away from restraint-based approaches in which sectors?
mcqs.e: Companion animal and zoological sectors have shifted toward reducing fear/stress.

mcqs.q: According to the equine behaviourists interviewed, horse caregivers are generally:
o: Extremely poor at recognising fear and anxiety
mcqs.e: Behaviourists reported caregivers are extremely poor at recognising fear/anxiety.

mcqs.q: When clients do recognise fear/anxiety, they tend to notice:
o: Only overt signs like rearing and running away
mcqs.e: Clients recognised overt signs but missed subtle ones like facial tension.

mcqs.q: What analytic method was applied to the semi-structured interviews?
mcqs.e: Interviews were analysed using thematic analysis.

mcqs.q: The most commonly reported environmental enrichment for ferrets included:
o: Hammocks, tunnels and tactile interaction with caretakers
mcqs.e: Hammocks, tunnels, and tactile caretaker interaction were most commonly reported.

mcqs.q: What was a frequently reported problem with ferret enrichment?
o: Ingestion of unsuitable chew/rubber items causing internal blockages
mcqs.e: Ingesting unsuitable chew/rubber items could cause internal blockages.

mcqs.q: Which enrichment, rarely provided but reported enjoyable and harmless, did the authors recommend more often?
mcqs.e: Scent trails were rarely provided yet enjoyed and harmless, so recommended more.

mcqs.q: This review focused on which Domains of the Five Domains Model?
mcqs.e: The review covered only the first four physical/functional Domains.

mcqs.q: The four physical/functional Domains are nutrition, physical environment, health, and:
mcqs.e: The fourth physical/functional Domain is behavioural interactions.

mcqs.q: Per the Model, inferences about Domain 5 mental experiences are made:
o: On the basis of detailed knowledge from the first four Domains
mcqs.e: Mental-state inferences derive from detailed knowledge of the first four Domains.
